First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨2,-1,2⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y+2z+6 & =0 \\ z & =-x+\frac{y}{2}-3.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=-3.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-3)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-3⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-3⟩)\cdot ⟨2,-1,2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
